geometry_edits.rationale: Introduce a split-wing dominant mass to create a more legible public seam and reduce the sealed tower-prism reading.
Orient the split along the principal axis so the street-facing threshold can be clarified.
Create a modest public void between wings rather than an internally sealed bulk.
Keep a grounded connecting element so the composition remains one massing rule with a clear base relationship.
Lower the split-wing profile enough to better match neighborhood living scale while preserving a clear upper hierarchy.
Preserve a vertical taper for the upper mass so the section remains calm and legible.
Reduce the arraying effect to avoid repetitive tiers and to strengthen a single dominant gesture.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the dominant bent-bar with a split-wing mass so the street edge can open into a more legible public threshold instead of remaining a sealed prismatic object.
Reduce the aggressiveness of the bend so the dominant gesture becomes calmer and more street-scaled.
Slightly simplify the recursive bend so the mass reads as one dominant figure rather than a complicated sculptural extrusion.
Keep the taper vertical so the section remains a plausible upper hierarchy rather than a lateral distortion.
Tighten the upper reduction modestly to reinforce a calm top while preserving usable base mass.
Reduce repetition so the form does not read as a stacked array of similar slabs; the program needs one clear dominant body with one clear void/threshold.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent mass in several views, so gesture clarity is moderate, but the form is still dominated by a bulky bent-bar/tapered object rather than a clearly public neighborhood-ground response. The parcel seems generally contained and the silhouette is not incoherent, yet the mass is more tower-prism than active street building. The thick blue access edge is not answered with an obvious entry seam, court, or void; instead the mass appears comparatively sealed at ground and the void logic is internal and weakly articulated. Across views there is no obvious collision failure, but the section feels arbitrary for neighborhood living: the upper shape reads as a sculptural taper/cap rather than a calm, capacity-aware mixed-use section with a legible public threshold. Reference 1 supports prismatic tapering and stepped profile; reference 2 suggests a lower, clearer neighborhood base with a distinct threshold, which is more transferable to the brief.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is much taller and more tower-like than the candidate; do not copy the vertical emphasis or rely on a high-rise reading.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact prismatic mass with a clear tapered/stepped upper profile can support a mixed-use identity when the ground condition stays legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is more enclosed and sculptural; the reference’s straightforward box/canopy logic is only partially transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple low horizontal base with a distinct attached vertical marker can create a readable public threshold and neighborhood-scale presence.

warnings: Program fit is not strong enough for a hard pass because the visible mass does not convincingly express an active ground edge or a clear public void tied to the access frontage.
Do not reward the mass merely for being coherent in silhouette; the neighborhood-living brief needs a more legible street threshold and public ground figure.
